query: I'm writing tests for a Python project and keep reinventing how to structure shared setup, handle async code paths, and fake external calls — want the established idioms instead of guessing.
There's a website whose look I want to reuse — I need the actual underlying color values, spacing scale, and component styles pulled out, not just eyeballing it in devtools.
I want one consistent toolkit that covers everything from the first design doc through cleanup at the end of a feature, not a pile of one-off scripts for each stage.
Make sure new commits stay consistent with how the rest of this codebase is written before they land.
This function has grown into something nobody can hold in their head anymore — help me carve it back down to something readable.
The site feels sluggish to users but I don't actually know what's causing it — I need to find the real culprit and confirm the fix actually helped before I ship it.
this feature is way too big to build in one shot — help me carve it into pieces I can actually ship one at a time
I want to make sure nobody starts writing code on this feature until we've nailed down exactly what it's supposed to do, written down and agreed.
Make this deck look like it actually came from the company behind Claude — same colors, same type, no guessing at the palette.
I've got a recorded walkthrough and need to know exactly what happens on screen, plus what's being said, without watching the whole thing myself.
I need direct low-level control of a real browser process, not a wrapper library, and it should fix its own approach when a selector stops working instead of just failing.
I keep reaching for a library or writing custom code for things the language already gives me for free — push back and make me justify that before I add anything.

let a couple of different models each take an independent pass at this, then reconcile their answers into something better than either alone, without paying full price for the biggest model on everything
I need a tally of who showed up broken down by congregation, with variant spellings of the same place merged instead of double counting.
there's a pile of inbound messages about an upcoming event — tie each one to the right attendee record and prep a reply queued to go out
Before I can pull a single page, I need the API key and client wired up correctly.
Our app needs a built-in way to pull clean text and data out of arbitrary web pages as a shipped feature, not just for a one-off research task.
Get my whole web-data toolkit running in one shot — fetching pages, running searches, clicking through sites, and having the credentials already wired in.
how much of last sprint's pipeline time went to re-fixing stuff we broke ourselves versus real new work, and could we have caught it before pushing
the site feels slower since the last release and I want hard numbers proving it, before and after

Right after we push a release, I want something continuously watching the pages for anything going wrong — broken visuals, slow loads, new console errors — so we catch it before customers do, without re-running the whole release process.
Before you do anything that can't be undone, stop and check with me first, and keep a record of what changed along the way.
I'm picking this back up after a break and don't want to re-explain everything I already figured out — just get me back to where I left off.

We're starting from a blank slate visually — need a documented, defendable set of visual decisions the team can point back to later, based on what similar products do, instead of everyone guessing individually.
I can't decide what direction this should go in — generate a handful of different looks so I can compare them side by side and pick one.
I need to lock down merges to this branch until further notice — we just had an incident and nothing should land except the critical fix.

Before this plan moves forward I want the business case, the interface, the codebase, and how developers will feel using it all checked automatically, with a call made on each, without me sitting in on every single pass.

I need one system that can click through my app like a user, probe it for holes an attacker would find, try out a few different visual directions, and steer the whole build-to-ship process without me handing off between separate tools each step.
something's broken and I keep patching symptoms without ever figuring out what's actually going wrong — make me pin that down before touching code
Someone outside the team is going to ask how this project is doing — I need a quick current snapshot pulled from what's been shipped and what's still outstanding, not a deep-dive.
I have a rough startup idea and want someone to push back hard on it — is there really a market, why hasn't this been done, what's the smallest version I could test.
Before we commit to building this, I want someone to push back hard on whether we're taking on too much or too little from a business standpoint.
Before people start adopting this tool, I want to see the experience through a total newcomer's eyes, compared honestly against what competitors offer, with concrete next steps — not just a number.
The model keeps doing the wrong thing because my instructions to it are apparently open to interpretation — tighten them up before that happens again.
Click through the app like a real visitor, find what's actually broken, fix it yourself with real commits, and prove it's better than before.
before this lands I want two different AI reviewers to argue over it and catch security holes a single pass would miss
getting this project ready to go live for the first time — want the credentials and config squared away before anything ships
I want to take my current branch, make sure it's tested and merges cleanly, bump the version, log what changed, and get it queued for review — all as one step, not a deploy afterward.
Before we start planning this out, let's actually talk through the open questions and lock in the choices we're making so we're not starting from a blank slate.
I want a single repeatable loop that carries a raw idea from first conversation to live, tested, merged code without me stitching each stage together by hand.

Before we start building, I want someone with no memory of this conversation to look at what we're about to do with fresh eyes and confirm it still makes sense, after digging into whatever we don't fully understand yet.
Before we call this feature finished, go check it actually does what it's supposed to, and patch anything that's still broken.
Before I download anything, I want to peek inside a dataset — what fields it has, what its parts look like, and whether it contains certain text — without pulling the whole thing.
we're paying for the same or nearly-the-same LLM calls over and over and I want to avoid re-running a prompt when something close enough was already answered.
Help me design how a change moves from a build through staging into production, including how we'd back out if a release goes bad.

I want to simulate someone actually clicking through the whole signup-to-checkout flow across different browsers and catch anything that visually looks off compared to before, without me manually clicking through it every release.
need to screen a batch of candidate compounds computationally before anything touches a lab bench
want to try out a quantum algorithm idea without needing access to real quantum hardware

I've got a big batch of individual-cell gene expression readouts, full of noise and dropouts, and I need to sort them into biologically meaningful groups and see what's driving the differences between those groups.
I have relational data — things connected to other things — and want to train a model that predicts new connections or classifies the whole structure, not just tabular rows.
I want to load a pretrained language model, run inference on it, and fine-tune it on my own data, all in Python.
I need to move this PHP app from the previous major framework release to the newest one without breaking anything already running in production.
This bug is slippery and I keep patching symptoms — I won't touch the code again until I have a reliable, repeatable way to tell whether a change actually worked.

Our team keeps using different words for the same concept across the codebase and conversations, and it drifts over time — I want that kept aligned as the project evolves, not just a one-time cleanup.

Push me through this spec decision by decision, offering your own guess each time so I mostly just approve or correct, and dig into the code yourself instead of asking whenever you can find the answer there.
when we lock in a decision on this design, check it against the vocabulary we've already agreed on for this codebase and write it down as a record we can point back to
Half our modules are just thin pass-through layers that don't actually do much — find the worst offenders and help me redesign them into something more substantial.

I need a Husky pre-commit setup and a way to stop dangerous git commands from running, plus some throwaway practice-problem folders scaffolded — none of it fits our normal engineering or productivity skills.
building a coding course and need consistent folder layouts for each lesson's starter code and answer key
The productivity commands I installed for this toolkit don't work right until each repo has its own local setup done first — I need that wired up.
I want this one contributor's whole toolkit — not just the coding stuff, the personal-life routines too, not a subset
We've been going back and forth on this feature for an hour — turn everything we've settled on into one proper requirements doc and post it to the tracker.
split this plan into independent chunks people can grab off the backlog, and flag which ones need a human to weigh in versus which the agent can just run with
Different people on the team keep calling the same concept by different names in code and in conversation, and I want that pinned down into one agreed vocabulary everyone has to use.
I just said something and I can tell it didn't land the way I meant — I want to try explaining it again, differently.
One entry in the catalog points to a dead link and its rating doesn't actually match what's backing it up — I want that single item fixed with citations, not a whole sweep.
I found a bunch of candidate skills but haven't verified anything about them yet — park them somewhere flagged as unverified so a human can check before any of them go live.

Some entries in the registry seem to require steps that don't actually exist, and others aren't connected to anything at all — I need to know exactly where the structure breaks down and what order to fix it in.
What's the current buzz around this topic across forums, video, and prediction markets over the past month — I don't want to check five different sites myself.
Before we ship, run a full sweep on this screen — contrast, spacing, animation timing, whether a screen reader could even use it — not just my gut feeling.
These three code changes don't depend on each other — I want them worked on at the same time instead of one after the other to save wall-clock time.
Before I show this diff to anyone else, get a fresh set of eyes on it now so problems surface before they spread.

I want one consistent way to work a coding task end to end—figuring out what to build, breaking it into steps, running things in parallel where I can, and working through failures methodically instead of guessing—all under one discipline.
Before I write any fix, I want solid proof of what's actually broken and why, stripped down to the smallest case that shows it, not just a hunch.
don't want my in-progress changes clobbering the checkout I already have open for something else
Stop telling me 'this should work now' — actually run it and show me real output before you say it's fixed.
Before I write any code on this multi-step feature I want it broken into small pieces someone else could pick up independently, spelled out clearly first.
I want the model to pick up the pattern from a handful of examples I paste into the prompt, no retraining involved.
want the page to feel like the visitor is piloting through space as they move down it, no jump cuts between sections
My UI works fine but it screams 'built by an AI' — generic spacing, default everything — I need it to look like a real designer touched it.
not sure how a prop works in this programmatic video library and need to check the official reference instead of guessing
I've built out my video composition and now need to actually export the finished file — encoding, output format, and how long that final pass takes.
I need my vector store kept in sync across multiple machines in real time, with search results that don't all cluster around the same few answers.
need to point an automated browser at a page, click through a flow, and grab a screenshot as proof it worked
A bunch of background jobs finished running in parallel and I need their outputs pulled together in one place, with a clear read on which ones actually succeeded versus failed.

I want to keep the interactive reasoning conversation going in one place while shipping background jobs off to run elsewhere, and have the results flow back automatically without me babysitting each one.
I need to spin up a whole cloud-hosted swarm of agents, manage the platform and billing side, and also train distributed neural nets across it — as one connected system, not separately.
I need people to log in, get their own isolated environment spun up on demand, get billed for usage, and see it all listed for others to browse and pick from.
I want several agents to independently weigh in on a decision and have their votes combined into one answer that sticks around across sessions.
I want certain checks to run automatically at specific points in the agent's workflow — and some things to happen on a schedule when I'm not watching — without me manually triggering them each time.
want the agent to actually get better at this kind of task over many separate sessions, not just start fresh every time

My agent setup is a patchwork of separate tools for remembering things, talking to my repo host, and getting multiple agents to agree with each other — I want it all consolidated under one roof, fully caught up to the latest version.

I need to modernize an entire aging internal platform in one coordinated push — the interface, the internals, the data layer, and how it talks to other systems — rather than patching pieces separately over time.
want the multi-agent setup to remember what worked on past runs and adapt for this kind of task, not just spin up a blank network layout every time
I'm restructuring our system into cleanly separated business areas, each owning its own core objects and firing events when something important happens inside it, instead of one tangled shared model.
My agents currently have three different memory systems that don't talk to each other and I want them collapsed into one consistent layer.
I want to be able to ask how the pieces of this codebase actually connect to each other, not just get back text snippets that mention similar words.
Pull together API docs for every route in this backend, based on what's already annotated in the code.
